criteria.text: R-1: parseRecords parses each nonblank line and trims values, preserving records and keys. Confirm by: TC-1 exact example and trimming assertions; pass when both exact arrays match.

R-1: parseRecords rejects missing equals, empty or invalid keys and duplicate keys with SyntaxError naming the 1-based source line, and rejects non-string input with TypeError. Confirm by: TC-2 rejection assertions; pass when every error has its specified type and line number.
R-1: parseRecords carries its public contract docstring. Confirm by: exact text search; pass when the docstring is /** Parse a string into records; throws TypeError or line-numbered SyntaxError. */
R-1: select returns exact matching records in input order. Confirm by: TC-3 assertions against multiple matches, the requested example and no matches; pass when each exact array matches.
R-1: select rejects non-array records with TypeError. Confirm by: TC-4 rejection assertions; pass when the error is TypeError.
R-1: select carries its public contract docstring. Confirm by: exact text search; pass when the docstring is /** Select matching records in input order; throws TypeError for non-arrays. */

amendment.summary: R-1 concerns: S1 supplies parsing, validation, numbered errors and its contract; S2 supplies ordered selection, array validation and its contract. Reuse node:test and npm test; seeded prior strategy had no specific decision and is refined with an available unit layer. Node v26.12.1 and npm 12.2.1, node --test and npm test passed the two existing tests; no browser, service, state, fixture setup or teardown is involved. test/text.test.js and src/text.js supply the existing test and CommonJS style. test/records.test.js is to be authored by test stage; TC-1 through TC-4 use node:test and strict assertions. No lint, type or build is configured. Match contract: src/text.js:1-7 uses strict mode, CommonJS exports, a concise public contract and TypeError; test/text.test.js:1-5 uses node:test, node:assert and named tests. New functions are public exports in local Node namespace, src/records.js is absent, and importing the module proves resolution; no persistence or migration. Assumption: split field at its first equals so remaining equals belong to the value; keys are validated as written. Exact source-check fixture comes from R-1. S1 diagnostics identify source line without echoing input; S2 throws TypeError for non-arrays. Baseline supplies runner; S1 supplies module to S2, both proofs run independently of future tests; test stage supplies durable focused cases for later regression. No other consumers or unresolved prerequisites found. Planning reference: docs/shiploop/w1-plan-reference.md; the focused suite must execute all four named cases, and the test stage owns authoring and revalidation. Backchain structural checker expects a different graph schema; its schema refusal is recorded in evidence_refs. This serial step-plan has no separate execution graph; dependency walk is documented in the planning reference. Send-back amendment: classify the C3/C6 source search as a check, retaining the focused test runner and regression rows. S1 is completed; E1 now records its working parser and E3 the existing parser test file. All other criteria, steps, command and layer rows are carried over. npm test revalidated five baseline tests in the current worktree; the test stage must restore TC-3 and TC-4 and revalidate all four IDs. The selector source is present as an uncommitted S2 change. No lint, type or build command is configured; the source search is a separate contract check.
